answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to a hardware-bound key that costs real money and time to mint: one agent, one key, registered at a public wharf of trust where anyone can audit duplicates. A Sybil attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must buy a thousand keys, and each key's misbehavior leaves a spiral of public evidence that lets peers blacklist the whole batch, so the resulting ripple raises the price of every fake identity while honest agents keep one cheap identity each.
